subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class core Agent Bundle import/export contract now, route this through plugin/ClawHub bundle APIs first, or defer until backup/profile portability work settles?
rationale: The feature is useful but chooses a durable portability format across stable CLI/RPC surfaces and security-sensitive state boundaries, which automation cannot safely decide from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design core bundle contract
options.body: Create a core-owned non-secret Agent Bundle design before implementation, with explicit allowlists and upgrade/security proof.

options.title: Route through plugin/ClawHub APIs
options.body: Keep core lean and first identify the missing plugin or bundle API surface needed for an external bundle implementation.

options.title: Defer behind portability program
options.body: Hold this issue until backup, profile export/import, and workspace sharing work converge on one migration story.

recommendation.title: Design core bundle contract
recommendation.body: Create a core-owned non-secret Agent Bundle design before implementation, with explicit allowlists and upgrade/security proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent agent/gateway maintenance plus broad current-main ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the product/security contract decision.
